neighbours.label: someone being told or notified of a piece of news, or having learned it (informed X of, told her about, announced that, learned that, a notice of), as opposed to other actions with the same people and frames, and to telling someone what to do
fire: The airline informed passengers of the delay at the gate.
The bank notified customers of the change in fees.
She was shocked when her sister told her about the divorce.
After the club announced that its coach would quit, the fans marched.
Last week, Anna learned that her job was gone.
The tenants received a notice of eviction on Monday.
He found out that his brother had sold the farm.
The doctor broke the news to the family on Friday.
quiet: The airline fed passengers on the plane at the gate.
The bank charged customers for the change in fees.
She was shocked when her sister told her to leave the house.
After the club closed for the summer, the fans marched.
Last week, Anna painted her flat green.
The tenants received a box of apples on Monday.
He stood outside while his brother sold the farm.
The doctor told a long joke to the family on Friday.

short: someone being told news, or having learned it
notes: Card: ' of' x5, ' announced' x4, ' told' x3, ' him', ' learned', ' them', from news text. Probes: 'told him' 1.00, 'announced' 0.62-1.01, 'notified shareholders of' 0.90, 'notice of' 0.54-0.71, 'informed the family of' 0.66, 'alerted employees of' 0.61, 'gave her the bad news' 0.41, 'learned' 0.39, 'found out' 0.34; 'paid employees for' 0.00, 'walked out' 0.09, 'bought a horse' 0.02, 'shipment of gravel' 0.04. Not everything fits: 'told him to wash the car' 0.48 (no news), 'told a long story' 0.20, 'discovered that' 0.06, and plain 'said that' 0.03, so saying alone is not enough, and telling without news is not silent.
